SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.74
EXPLANATION: The strong band at 2273 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a nitrile C≡N stretch, uniquely consistent with candidate 10 which has two C≡N groups; the presence of two high-frequency X–H stretches at 3225/3258 cm⁻¹ aligns with O–H (GFQ-001) and N–H (GFQ-002) stretches in CC(N)C(O)(C#N)C#N, with the lower OH frequency explained by hydrogen bonding (ENV-001). The intense aliphatic C–H stretches at 2928/2985 cm⁻¹ match GFQ-003, the 1458 cm⁻¹ CH₃ scissoring and multiple 930–970 cm⁻¹ bands fit NH wag/rocking modes (GFQ-002), and the 1588 cm⁻¹ band can be attributed to NH₂ bending (GFQ-002). The 1185–1205 cm⁻¹ region is consistent with C–O/C–N fingerprint modes expected for a tertiary alcohol adjacent to nitriles. Overall, candidate 10 best explains the nitrile, OH, NH, and aliphatic features observed.
